html:
Bogotá is the capital of Colombia, on a high plateau of the eastern Andes. The Spanish conquistador Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada founded it on 6 August 1538 in the land of the Muisca.

It grew as the seat of the Audiencia and, from the 1700s, of the Viceroyalty of New Granada, with convents, a cathedral and colleges. Its isolation in the mountains, many days' travel from the coast, made it a city of lawyers and clerics, and it was proud to be called the Athens of South America.

Bogotá was the capital of Gran Colombia under Bolívar and then of Colombia. It was largely burned in the Bogotazo of 1948 and grew in the late 1900s into a city of millions, many of them people fleeing violence in the countryside.
